title: Redaction benchmark composition design (#1185)
rationale: A robust redaction bench needs three difficulty tiers, each answering a different question, weighted by the research risk ranking (see memory redaction-hard-structures-research). EASY = calibration floor (collateral/false-positive baseline; every tool should pass). MEDIUM = geometry/encoding on the CORRECT carrier (shift, partial removal, collateral — where excise's #942 line-stepping lived). HARD = carrier leaks + corruption/rendering risk (where reference tools fail and excise's #636/#608/#1182 leaks lived). Coverage floor is >=3 per structure type to see a pattern, 5 for research top-risk types. Real-doc cases live in tests/redaction-hard-cases.tsv; synthetic one-carrier-in-isolation fixtures live in the redaction-adversarial generator.

sources.real: tests/redaction-hard-cases.tsv — publicly available real-world PDFs from the gitignored corpora (federal gov forms, pdfjs/pdfium/poppler/ghent/altona/pdfua/verapdf). Path + term checked in; PDFs are corpus, absent skips.
sources.synth: scripts/gen-adversarial-redaction-corpus.py — test-pdfs/redaction-adversarial/, one controlled fixture per carrier in isolation.

excluded.encrypted: On hold since 2026-08-25 (no new encrypted-redaction work or bench axis). The reference adapters take (src,dst,term) with no password, so encrypted rows would be adapter-failed rows measuring nothing.
excluded.width-fingerprint: Deferred. The de-redaction glyph-width side channel is the research #1 unhardened gap, but the bench has no axis that can measure it (byte/oracle/collateral/ink are blind to it) — fixtures would read clean on every tool. Needs a dedicated residue-recovery gate (ResidueRecoveryEngine), filed separately.

easy.purpose: Calibration floor — collateral / false-positive baseline. Every tool should pass. Terms MUST be single-carrier (byte occurrences <= visible occurrences) so a leak here is a real defect, not a hidden copy.

easy-plain-body.note: Type1/standard-14 body-text word (scarce in real PDFs — most embed TrueType)

easy-multi-occurrence.note: term appears 3-10x; remove all, damage none

medium.purpose: Geometry/encoding stress on the CORRECT carrier — text is in page content but positioning/encoding makes clean glyph removal hard.

cid-type0.note: Type0/CID multi-byte; byte offset != char index

tj-kerning-heavy.note: word split across many TJ pieces

stacked-overlapping.note: text drawn twice at same position (scarce real; synthetic-backed)

small-glyph.note: very small font size / fine print

type3-font.note: Type3 font — glyphs are content-stream CharProcs, not a simple Tj to drop

rotated-page.note: /Rotate 90/180/270 — page rotation, redaction box must transform

clipped-text.note: text under an active clipping path (W/W*) — bbox vs visible mismatch

vertical-cjk.note: vertical writing mode (WMode 1) CJK — advance is along y, not x

hard.purpose: Carrier leaks + corruption/rendering risk — the secret survives in a carrier the tool did not scrub, or removal corrupts the file.

actualtext-inline.note: /ActualText inline in a BDC property list (rare in real docs; mostly synthetic)

invisible-text.note: render mode 3 Tr / OCR layer (only 3 in corpus; synthetic-backed)

shared-form-xobject.note: Form XObject Do'd from >1 page with the term INSIDE the shared form. Shared forms are common in real corpora, but tying a clean redaction term to the shared form's content (vs page body) is not reliably verifiable across qpdf object renumbering — covered by a controlled synthetic fixture.

image-baked-text.note: secret ONLY as pixels in a rasterised image (scan/baked graphic) — no text layer; findable only by OCR of the rendered page. Measured by the ImageBakedReadable axis (#1185).

no-tounicode.note: subset font glyphs with NO /ToUnicode — extraction blind spot; term may not be recoverable as text at all

contents-array.note: page /Contents is an ARRAY of streams; an operator/BT may span the boundary

scarcity_note: Some structures are genuinely rare in publicly-available test corpora (Type1 body text, inline /ActualText, shared Form XObjects, real /Alt, stacked-overlapping text, invisible OCR layers — only 3 exist corpus-wide). For those the design target reflects what public corpora can supply, and each carrier is additionally covered by a controlled synthetic fixture in the redaction-adversarial generator. Targets were NOT inflated to force 100%: gaps are documented scarcity, not silent.
